resources_retrieved.title: NCERT Class 10 Science - Chapter 1: Chemical Reactions and Equations
resources_retrieved.publisher: National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)
resources_retrieved.subject: Science
resources_retrieved.excerpt: A complete chemical equation represents the reactants, products and their physical states symbolically. A chemical equation is balanced so that the numbers of atoms of each type involved in a chemical reaction are the same on the reactant and product sides of the equation. Equations must always be balanced to satisfy the Law of Conservation of Mass: Mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction. Example: 3Fe(s) + 4H2O(g) -> Fe3O4(s) + 4H2(g).

resources_retrieved.title: NCERT Class 10 Science - Chapter 1: Chemical Reactions and Equations
resources_retrieved.publisher: National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)
resources_retrieved.subject: Science
resources_retrieved.excerpt: In a combination reaction two or more substances combine to form a new single substance. Decomposition reactions are opposite to combination reactions: a single substance decomposes to give two or more substances. Reactions in which heat is given out along with the products are called exothermic reactions. Reactions in which energy is absorbed are known as endothermic reactions. When an element displaces another element from its compound, a displacement reaction occurs: Fe(s) + CuSO4(aq) -> FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s). Two compounds exchange ions to form two new compounds in a double displacement reaction: Na2SO4(aq) + BaCl2(aq) -> BaSO4(s) + 2NaCl(aq).

resources_retrieved.title: NCERT Class 10 Science - Chapter 2: Acids, Bases and Salts
resources_retrieved.publisher: National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)
resources_retrieved.subject: Science
resources_retrieved.section: 2.1 Understanding the Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
resources_retrieved.excerpt: Acids are sour in taste and change the colour of blue litmus to red. Bases are bitter and change the colour of red litmus to blue. Litmus solution is a purple dye extracted from lichen. When an acid reacts with a metal, hydrogen gas is evolved and a corresponding salt is formed: Acid + Metal -> Salt + Hydrogen gas. For example, 2HCl + Zn -> ZnCl2 + H2. When acids react with metal carbonates or hydrogen carbonates, carbon dioxide gas is produced: Na2CO3 + 2HCl -> 2NaCl + H2O + CO2.
